A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. The text, equations, five figures, dataset table, and Appendices A–D are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: Section 4 reports original diagonal-loading and step-size experiments, plus subgraph-density and runtime comparisons on six real-world networks.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original graph-mining experiments, revises plotted results, and additionally reports integral convergence within the stated iteration budget.

M1.justification: The diagonal-loading objective, Frank–Wolfe updates and step-size options, and constraint parameterization solved with AdamW are retained. The added quickselect discussion concerns an equivalent implementation of the existing top-k operation.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same densest-k-subgraph task on Facebook, web-Stanford, com-Youtube, soc-Pokec, as-Skitter, and com-Orkut. Table 1 statistics and the plotted subgraph-size coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Figure 5 includes Greedy in the Facebook runtime comparison in v2 but omits its curve and legend entry in v3. Other comparator membership is retained, including the existing omission of Greedy from Facebook's density panel.

E3.justification: Section 4.3 increases Frank–Wolfe's reported iteration cap for baseline comparisons fivefold, from 200 to 1,000, while AdamW remains at 200. This substantially revises the optimization budget underlying the main density/runtime comparisons. Other stated settings remain stable; the PDFs do not establish the rerun history.

E4.justification: Figure 2 revises the λ = 0.1 traces in the existing Facebook diagonal-loading sensitivity experiment, particularly solution sparsity. The tested loading values and analytical question remain unchanged, and Figure 3's step-size experiment is retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty bands for its experimental results.

E6.justification: Figure 5 revises runtime curves across the six networks, notably Frank–Wolfe's relative efficiency: on com-Youtube it now exceeds EXPP's runtime at some larger k. These results accompany a revised iteration cap, so they do not establish a same-setting slowdown. Figure 2's λ = 0.1 sparsity at iteration 200 changes from approximately 0.29 to 0.36, and Section 4.3 newly reports integral convergence within 1,000 iterations. Figure 4's density results are largely retained.

T1.justification: Appendix B corrects stationarity calculations to use the loaded objective g instead of f and derives g(x'') − g(x*) = 2λt², repairing a central proof step. Appendices A and C correct edge-term subtractions. Section 3.3 changes the Frank–Wolfe complexity bound from O(m + k log n) to O(m + n + k log n) and adds an average O(m + n) bound using quickselect. The theorem conclusions remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims remain the λ = 1 tightness threshold, the effect of loading on local maxima, two projection-free solution approaches, and strong density/scalability performance. The expanded discussion of the AAAI predecessor explains contributions already present in v2.

C2.justification: Section 4.6 qualifies the explanation attributing AdamW's higher cost to PyTorch versus NumPy as particularly relevant under CPU-only execution. The existing landscape interpretations, loading tradeoffs, and tightness limitations are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 adds quickselect as an implementation option for top-k selection, and Section 4.3 revises the documented iteration limits. Hardware, initialization, preprocessing, AdamW's learning rate, and the code URL remain unchanged; the URL is relocated.

R1.justification: V3 adds Matula and Beck (1983) for k-core peeling and expands the comparison with the cited AAAI paper, explicitly discussing its restricted tightness guarantee and the reuse of Theorems 3 and 4. The remaining cited works are retained despite reference reordering and metadata updates.

P1.justification: The introduction and related-work prose are revised, the AAAI comparison is expanded, and Section 2 gains separate tightness and landscape-analysis subsections. Most method, experimental, and appendix prose and the overall section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: The entire document changes from an IEEE two-column layout to a single-column layout, with different margins, equation flow, algorithm formatting, table-caption placement, and figure placement and sizing. Figures 2, 4, and 5 are redrawn with revised title, axes, and legend arrangements; the same five figures and dataset table remain.

improvement.justification: V3 repairs an important deficiency in the theoretical foundation: Appendix B now applies stationarity to the objective actually being maximized and supplies the missing valid derivation. Together with the corrected rounding/local-maximizer proof expansions and complexity bounds, this substantially strengthens support for the central guarantees. Revised iteration and runtime reporting also makes the empirical evidence clearer, although the larger budget prevents interpreting changed timings as same-setting performance gains.
